question: With episode trace flushing fixed, does the existing frequency/late retention reduce complete-request cost relative to none/early release8 after all extra grouping and lifecycle costs?
basis: Late ordering attains its fixed-protected-set current-call group lower bound and lowers payload; old timing was inconclusive. A separate lifecycle intervention reduced observed GC cost, without proving old mechanism gains.
workload: Same3 documents P32/P32/P128, outputs16/16/8; inject new request after4 old outputs; release chunk8 only after both old requests complete
intervention: Existing current-layer frequency protected set, loaded late; default none/early is the strongest measured complete-request baseline. Selector, capacity, kernel and precision unchanged; all policies independently execute their future state.
reset: Existing drained pager metadata reset plus same five warmups. Each measured episode is drained before all its and warmup records/events are written/released. Allocations/KV free queue preserved, KV contents not compared.
primary: Complete capture wall including in-window observations plus old per-request max-ITL/completion and new TTFT/completion; preserve the full tradeoff, no selected scalar SLO.

accounting.per_repeat: From before GPU preflight/reset through all warmups, requests, snapshots/raw writes and flush/decref. Excludes its own cycle_progress write and shared final tail; both are covered by whole engine cycle/process.
accounting.engine: Post-init cycle through shutdown, with own final marker covered by parent process wall. Mixed-policy engine totals are total cost, not attributable arm speedups. Tar/readback outside these clocks.
accounting.gc: Observed callback intervals only; observer closes before event export/shutdown. Never subtract GC or sum overlapping CUDA/CPU spans.

comparison: Within each engine adjacent pairs (0,1),(2,3),(4,5),(6,7), oriented frequency versus none; report all 8 pairs, order, per-engine mode summaries and same-mode repeats. No observed max-delta used as a noise bound.
integrity: All measurement/warmup requests retained; consecutive global call IDs across flushes; row/request/time joins; source/GPU boundary checks; actual resources and common logical pre-action state. Compare trace equality within mode, not across distinct policies.
qualification: No numerical or grouping implementation changed; inherits prior bounded frequency/late single-layer qualification. This is not full-model task quality validation.
stop: Foreign GPU process/query failure, incomplete requests or corrupt evidence abort and retain files. No automatic retry or additional outcome-selected runs.
interpretation: Consistent benefit across order and both engines with preserved old-request progress supports another independent workload evaluation, not method GO. If bytes fall but complete requests do not improve, retain the group/transfer tradeoff and narrow this formulation; do not falsify the problem family. Unresolved pre-action drift remains a measurement limitation.
ceiling: Two engines on same three documents, single-model/artificial expert cap native eager paging. Dependent episodes; no population significance, production p99/SLO, quality or general novelty claim.
cpu_checks: Runner syntax and two invalid CLI combinations checked before GPU. Pager/grouping numerical implementation unchanged from previously qualified and tested lifecycle sources.
